subject.title: Browser backend plugin interface (support third-party drivers via MCP/custom adapter)

question: Should OpenClaw expose a generic browser backend Plugin SDK/registry seam for third-party drivers, or keep browser backends limited to first-party profile drivers for now?
rationale: The requested seam would become public API for browser-control authority and profile configuration, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent driver contract, trust boundary, or upgrade policy.

options.title: Design Generic SDK Registry
options.body: Add a versioned backend contract, registry-owned driver ids, config/schema/client/runtime routing, docs, and security tests before accepting third-party adapters.

options.title: Limit To First-Party Drivers
options.body: Keep solving Browserbase, extension relay, and My Browser needs as built-in or bundled-plugin drivers without exposing a general third-party contract yet.

options.title: Defer Until Narrow PRs Settle
options.body: Keep this issue open while narrower browser work clarifies the minimum safe registration API.

recommendation.title: Design Generic SDK Registry
recommendation.body: Add a versioned backend contract, registry-owned driver ids, config/schema/client/runtime routing, docs, and security tests before accepting third-party adapters.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the newest merged work on the same browser driver surface and already scoped this issue as a Plugin SDK design gap.
